subject: ECON 140: Essay 2 draft due Thursday, Nov 5
body:
Hi everyone,

A quick note on Essay 2 (the defaults-and-nudges essay). Your full draft, 1,500 to 2,000 words, is due on Canvas by Thursday, November 5 at 11:59 pm. This is the version you'll exchange with a peer reviewer, so it should be a complete argument, not an outline. Rough edges are fine; missing sections are not.

A few reminders:
- Pick ONE real-world default (retirement auto-enrollment, organ donor registration, cafeteria layout, and so on) and evaluate it using at least two of the frameworks from weeks 6 to 8.
- Cite the course readings by author and page. Outside sources are welcome but optional.
- Put your section number in the filename.

If you're stuck choosing a topic, come to office hours or post in the discussion board. Looking forward to reading these.

Best,
Prof. Brandt-Okoye

subject: Announcement: Homework 7 and final project proposals
body:
Dr. Owen Castellanos-Reid posted an announcement in STAT 121: Applied Regression:

Two things for your calendar, so please read to the end.

1) Homework 7 (interaction terms and residual diagnostics) is posted. It is due Thursday, November 5 at 11:59 pm. Submit a single PDF rendered from your notebook; screenshots of code will not be graded.

2) Final project proposals are due Monday, November 16 at 9:00 am. Work in groups of 2 or 3. The proposal is one page: your question, your dataset (with a link), the outcome variable, and at least three candidate predictors. One person submits for the whole group and lists everyone's names at the top.

We'll spend part of section next week brainstorming datasets, so don't panic if you don't have one yet.

Dr. Castellanos-Reid

subject: Reminder: Summer 2027 Data Science Internship applications close Nov 4
body:

subject: Announcement: Problem Set 5 (Hash Tables) is posted
body:
Prof. Imogen Vasquez-Hale posted an announcement in CS 152: Data Structures and Systems:

Good morning! Problem Set 5 is now up on Canvas under Assignments. This one is all about hash tables: you'll implement a hash map with linear probing (including deletion with tombstones and resizing), then run a small experiment measuring probe counts as the load factor grows.

It's due next Friday at 5:00 pm, so you have a full week. Submit your code and your experiment write-up together through the course portal. The usual late policy applies: you have three late days for the semester, and each one is 24 hours.

Starter code is in the ps5 folder of the course repo. Please pull before you start; we fixed a typo in the test file this morning.

See you Tuesday!

subject: Colloquium Thu 11/5: Small Models, Big Pipelines
body:
Please join us for this week's Computer Science Colloquium.

Small Models, Big Pipelines: Orchestrating Local Language Models on a Laptop
Dr. Lucia Ferraro-Quinn, Fennwick Institute of Computing
Thursday, November 5, 4:00 to 5:15 pm
Brannock Hall, Room 105

Abstract: Much of the excitement around language models focuses on ever-larger systems in the cloud. This talk goes the other direction: how far can you get with several small models running locally, each doing one narrow job? I will describe experiments in which teams of small models extract, check, and summarize information, and discuss where these pipelines fail and how to catch those failures cheaply.

Refreshments will be served before the talk. Undergraduates are especially welcome, and no RSVP is needed.

subject: Action required: Spring 2027 Housing Intent Form due Nov 13
body:

If you are planning to study away in the spring, you will also need to upload your program acceptance letter once it arrives; that upload does not need to happen by the 13th.

Thank you,

subject: Following up: pass/fail option for HIST 97
body:
Hi Riley,

It was good to talk on Friday. Following up on your question about HIST 97: yes, you can switch it to pass/fail, and since it isn't counting toward your concentration, it won't affect your requirements. You could also drop it entirely and still be enrolled full time with three courses this term, though I'd only recommend that if the workload is truly unmanageable.

Either way, the deadline is Tuesday, November 10 at 5:00 pm. That is the last day to drop a course without a W on your transcript or to change a course to pass/fail. Both changes are made in the Student Portal under "Enrollment Changes," and neither needs my signature.

Let me know what you decide, or if you want to talk it through again before then.

Best,
Dr. Holt-Delacroix

subject: Project Milestone 2 due this Sunday (Nov 8)
body:
Good morning, project teams!

A reminder that Project Milestone 2 is due this Sunday, November 8 at 11:59 pm. For this milestone, each team should submit:

1. A link to your repository with a working prototype of your key-value store (get, put, and delete should all work; persistence is not required yet).
2. A two-page write-up with a benchmark comparing your store against a plain Python dict for at least two workload sizes.
3. A short paragraph on how you split the work.

Only one person per team needs to submit. If your team is still deciding which collision strategy to use, Thursday's lecture on hash tables and Problem Set 5 should help, but don't wait until PS5 is finished to start on the benchmark.

Reply here or post on the course forum if you have questions.

Priya
